findings.title: Return pooled connections when connection setup fails
findings.why_it_matters: After getconn() checks a connection out, a failure while assigning its isolation level or during BaseDatabaseWrapper.connect() setup leaves that connection checked out. Repeated setup failures can consume the pool's available slots, causing otherwise healthy callers to time out waiting for a connection.
evidence: django/db/backends/base/base.py:256-258: `self.connection = self.get_new_connection(conn_params)` is followed by `self.set_autocommit(...)` and `self.init_connection_state()` without cleanup if either raises.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the pooled checkout and all subsequent connection initialization in cleanup handling: if setup raises, return the checked-out connection to its originating pool (or discard it if unusable), clear the wrapper's connection reference, and re-raise.

testing_gaps: Exercise an exception after pool.getconn() succeeds (including a failure in set_autocommit()) and verify the slot becomes available to another wrapper.
